arizona.summary: General Order 26-09 creates immigration-habeas assignment, service and briefing procedures, subject to the assigned judge.
requirements: Consent to magistrate jurisdiction is voluntary; paper pro se petitions without consent go to a district judge. The United States has consented subject to withdrawal under the order.

The clerk serves the USAO and issues a schedule: appearance in 3 calendar days, answer in 7 calendar days; reply in 3 calendar days for represented petitioners or 14 days from service for self-represented petitioners. The assigned judge may modify it.
Dismissal arguments belong in the answer. A TRO application must be separate and comply with Rule 65; it does not suspend the habeas briefing schedule.

The government must give at least two business days’ notice before removal from the United States during proceedings. The order provides automatic substitution of the facility warden when a proper respondent was omitted.

california-central.summary: General Order 26-05 supplies a standard immigration-habeas schedule and special TRO, service and removal-notice procedures.
requirements: The clerk serves the USAO and issues notice: appearance in 3 calendar days; answer in 7 calendar days; reply in 3 calendar days after filing the answer for represented petitioners, or 14 days after service for pro se petitioners. Judge may modify.
Put dismissal arguments in the answer rather than a separate motion. File TRO applications separately under Federal Rule 65 and Local Rules 65-1 and 7-19; filing one does not suspend briefing.
The government must give at least two court days’ notice before removing a petitioner from the Central District during the case.
Magistrate consent is voluntary. Appointed §2241 counsel receive a limited admission/pro hac vice fee waiver.

colorado.summary: The court’s posted §2241 instructions impose a 30-page application limit and specific formatting and service requirements.
requirements: Absent prior court order, the application including attachments answering questions may not exceed 30 pages. Type or write legibly on one-sided 8½×11-inch paper with1½-inch top margin and1-inch other margins.
Sign each form. Submit the original application and keep a copy. Papers other than the original application require a certificate stating the date/address of service on respondents or counsel.

Pay$5 or use the proper IFP motion/affidavit. The instructions discuss prisoner institutional-account certificates; check the distinct civil-immigration situation before applying prisoner-specific requirements.

sources.label: Posted §2241 instructions, revisionAugust 24,2015
sources.reviewStatus: Relevant operative text read

limitations: Posted instructions expressly include immigration claims but contain old INS terminology. Current statutory jurisdiction and local amendments require separate review.

oregon.summary: Local Rule 81-1 expressly includes §2241 and requires court-supplied forms and verification.
requirements: Petitions under §2241 must be legibly written or typed on court-supplied forms, signed under penalty of perjury by the petitioner or an authorized person, with the original sent to the clerk.

For a prisoner seeking IFP, LR 81-1 requires financial affidavit/declaration and an institutional-account certificate. Check immigration-specific applicability and court instructions before applying prisoner-account requirements to civil detainees.

pennsylvania-eastern.summary: The September 2026 immigration-specific instructions provide a local packet, warden naming, clerk service and court-set briefing.
requirements: Type or neatly write, answer all questions, and sign/date under penalty of perjury. Hard copies use one-sided 8½×11-inch paper; relevant immigration documents may be attached.
For a detained petitioner name the facility warden; if unknown the instructions permit “Warden of [facility]”.
Include the $5 fee or signed habeas IFP application. Mail to the Clerk, 601 Market Street, Room 2609, Philadelphia PA 19106, attention Immigration Habeas.
After legal review the court arranges service if not already accomplished and sets response/reply deadlines. Report contact changes in writing; failure can cause dismissal.

texas-southern.summary: The court’s immigration-habeas guidance specifies divisional filing and restricted electronic access for non-attorneys.
requirements: File with the clerk’s divisional office covering the county where the detention facility is physically located. Sending a petition to the USAO does not file it and the USAO will not forward it.
Non-attorney parties need the presiding judge’s approval before registering for electronic filing access.
Temporary electronic filing privileges are unavailable for emergencies. The court recommends expedited delivery and clearly identifying the emergency request.
Filing fees go to the clerk. Processing may occur after receipt; the clerk or PACER can provide the case number. A wrong-division filing will generally be processed and transferred.

texas-western.summary: The court requires separate motions and warns against sending petitions to the USAO; emergency electronic privileges are unavailable.
requirements: Mail to the appropriate divisional clerk. A petition mailed to the USAO is not filed or forwarded. Pending pro hac vice admission, the listed filing options are mail or in person.
No temporary electronic privileges for emergency filings; guidance recommends overnight delivery with a cover letter identifying the emergency.
The court asks for the A-number, detainee’s signature, and fee or IFP application. Its guidance says pro se next-friend submissions also need the detainee’s signature.
File a TRO or other motion as a separate document, not inside the petition.

For cases assigned to Judge Xavier Rodriguez, the October 23,2026 order stays government response deadlines for immigration petitions asserting a substantive due-process right to freedom from § 1225(b)(2)(A) custody during immigration proceedings, pending further order. This is claim- and judge-specific.

utah.summary: General Order 26-005 authorizes provisional federal-defender representation for qualifying immigration detainees.
requirements: The individual must contact the Federal Public Defender, be detained in immigration custody within Utah, appear financially eligible, and have a colorable §2241 claim.
The defender may screen, investigate and file appropriate petitions/motions. Filing fee is provisionally waived for petitions prepared under this appointment; defender also files IFP motion.
The assigned judge reviews financial eligibility and interests of justice and can request information, require payment or rescind appointment.

washington-western.summary: The court supplies a dedicated pro se immigration packet for Northwest ICE Processing Center, separate from non-immigration habeas.
requirements: Use the immigration packet for detention at Northwest ICE Processing Center. Mail hard copies to 700 Stewart Street, Suite 2310, Seattle WA 98101, or use the packet’s stated electronic route; use one-sided 8½×11-inch paper.
Sign/date under penalty of perjury, remove identifying information as directed, and pay $5 or submit the habeas IFP application.
The packet normally lists the warden and specified federal officials as respondents; follow the local instructions rather than importing another district’s respondent list.
Court notifies respondents and sets briefing; magistrate consent is voluntary. The packet includes a counsel application, without guaranteeing appointment.

west-virginia-southern.summary: The court directs filers to substitute its local §2241 instructions for the national AO242 cover instructions.
requirements: The local instructions expressly include illegal immigration detention and distinguish final removal-order review. Use one-sided 8½×11-inch paper, sign, answer all questions and number any continuation pages.
Put any brief/legal argument in a separate memorandum. Send available challenged decisions, briefs and administrative-remedy forms with the petition.

Pay$5 or submit the court IFP form with the institutional financial certificate described in the instructions. Mail the original, retain a copy and promptly report transfer/release or address changes.
The judge determines whether an answer is required; no automatic default response deadline is promised.
